title: Capacity oncall handoff and action-item runbook - 2026-05-09
content:
Context / purpose:
This doc captures the mid-sprint capacity oncall handoff notes, the lightweight runbook we used during yesterday’s triage, and the action-items we agreed to carry through the next two sprints. Goal: make handoffs predictable, reduce mean time to capacity-adjust, and codify short-term mitigations for region spikes. This is a working note — most items are rough and actionable.

Attendance (virtual huddle 2026-05-09 09:15 PT):
- Maya Chen (owner, infra capacity)
- Ibrahim Torres (SRE, fleet orchestration)
- Rachel Nguyen (infra, regional ops)
- Samir Patel (platform eng, autoscaler)
- Lena Ortiz (release eng, deploy safety)
- Oncall: rotation-2 (pager duty) joined for the first 30m

High level status (current signal):
- Global GPU utilization: 72% avg, 95th p90=95% in eu-west-1 during 08:00-09:00 UTC window.
- Queued inference requests (hosted API): 14k total, spike in long-tail (>1s scheduling) ~2.1k requests queued in eu-west-1.
- Tail token latency: median 88ms, p99 (regional) eu-west-1 = 1.2s, ap-southeast-1 = 950ms.
- Minor preemption noise in us-west-2 due to a local maintenance job (noticed higher scheduling retry count).
- No customer-visible SLA violations yet; several internal alerts fired for scheduling latency.

Incidents / signals observed this week (compact):
- 2026-05-07 22:40 UTC: short-lived scheduling backlog in eu-west-1 after a canary deploy for the v2 autoscaler (INF-4231). Root cause: bad backpressure filter settings — autoscaler introduced small throttle window. Mitigation: rollback canary, reapply with adjusted filter (done, queue drained in 5m).
- 2026-05-08 03:15 UTC: preemption surge in ap-southeast-1 due to noisy neighbor on spot cluster; prewarm deficit visible for T4p instances. Mitigation: temporarily pinned critical routes to dedicated pool (config change) — action item to add soft-reserve logic.

Oncall handoff checklist (condensed, for 1pm handoff):
1) Dashboard sanity: check per-region GPU utilization, queue depth, and preemption rate.
2) Verify autoscaler health: check controller logs for error bursts and backpressure counters.
3) Confirm capacity headroom matrix: dedicated vs. shared pool reserves (sheet: capacity-reserves-2026-Q2).
4) Check scheduled jobs: any batch reclaims or maintenance windows in next 6 hours? If yes, notify ops and consider postponing.
5) If queue depth > 1k sustained for 5+ min in any region: escalate to oncall and follow mitigation steps below.

Quick mitigations (order matters):
- Step A: Reroute critical routes to dedicated pools with reserved slots (low friction, config change).
- Step B: Increase burst capacity (if quota available) in region for 20m, watch for downstream retries.
- Step C: If autoscaler is the source (recent deploy), roll back to last known-good, then re-evaluate.
- Step D: Apply cache warmers for hot prefixes (manual trigger via admin endpoint).
- Step E: If preemption/spot churn is causing failure, failover to on-demand/dedicated with soft reserve, and open INF ticket.

Action items accepted (owners + deadlines):
- Maya: Draft a simple soft-reserve design doc to allow critical routes to reserve N GPUs per region (prototype by 2026-05-16).
- Samir: Add telemetry hooks to autoscaler to expose backpressure-window histogram (PR + tests by 2026-05-14). Blocker: need env to run long tail test.
- Ibrahim: Create a burn-down runbook for queue draining using prioritized reroutes and cache priming (deliver by 2026-05-12).
- Rachel: Validate spare quota in sa-east-1 (Sao Paulo) and verify we can stand up 4 extra cards within 30m (report by 2026-05-13).
- Lena: Add a pre-deploy checklist entry for capacity-impacting autopatches and require one extra approver for autoscaler changes (policy update by 2026-05-17).

Capacity projection sketch (next 14 days):
- Baseline demand growth: +6–8% week over week observed across non-peak windows.
- Planned capacity adds: +10% in ap-northeast-1 (scheduled 2026-05-12), +5% in eu-west-1 (2026-05-15), contingent on quota approvals.
- Hedging plan: maintain 8% spare global headroom for unexpected spikes, shift 3% from low-util regions (us-east-1) via temporary reallocation.

Runbook excerpt: draining a regional queue (quick steps for oncall)
- Preconditions: verify oldest queued request age > 60s and queue depth > 1k for 10m.
- 1) Switch critical route(s) to dedicated-pool-A via feature flag (admin console).
- 2) Enable cache priming job for top-200 prefixes (api call: /admin/cache/prime).
- 3) Temporarily raise per-pod concurrency limit in region controller by +10% (safe window 20m).
- 4) Monitor: queue depth, scheduler latency, and p99 token latency. If no improvement in 10m, escalate to infra-leads and open INF-urgent ticket.

Experiments / low-risk trials planned:
- Soft-reserve experiment: prototype using a token-bucket style reservation to keep 5 GPUs warm per critical route in eu-west-1 for 48hr window. Goal: measure queue reduction and cost delta.
- Pre-warm jittering: small experiment to randomize warmers across 5m windows to avoid simultaneous warm bursts.
- Autoscaler canary ramp: new canary configuration to use 0.5s backpressure window vs previous 2s — run on 3% of traffic for one week.

Risks & unresolved questions:
- Point of failure: scheduler controller still has a tight coupling with backpressure heuristics — we need to decouple decisioning to a library to reduce rollback blast radius.
- Cost impact: soft reserves will increase short-term spend — need quick ROI threshold (suggested: queue reduction > 40% for routes with >10k qps).
- SLA exposure: if we route too aggressively to dedicated pools, other customers in that pool could see contention; propose a small safety quota for cross-swap.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider an "emergency fast-fail" flag that forces oldest requests to escape scheduling and route to fallback model variant (lower cost, lower accuracy) to protect user-facing apps.
- Build a lightweight test harness to replay production queue profiles into staging autoscaler to validate backpressure changes.

Links / references:
- INF-4231 (autoscaler canary rollback)
- Confluence: capacity-reserves-2026-Q2 (sheet)
- github: fleet PR 289 (autoscaler telemetry)

Next checkpoint: 2026-05-12 standup — we'll review soft-reserve prototype plan and telemetry PR status. If telemetry isn’t ready, defer canary.

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot at 2026-05-09 08:45 UTC:
- total_gpus_online: 14,920
- global_util_avg: 72%
- eu-west-1_util_p90: 95%
- queued_total: 14,000
- queued_over_60s: 1,540
- preemption_rate_1h: ap-southeast-1 = 0.8% (elevated)

End of note.

(If you are the receiving oncall, please ping in #infra-capacity with the subject "handoff-2026-05-09" and confirm you received this doc.)
